definition: Illustrative input-output pairs included in a prompt to demonstrate the desired task and format to a language model.
details: Well-chosen few-shot examples can substantially improve output quality and consistency by clarifying ambiguous instructions through demonstration rather than description alone.
story: Picture a novelist who has read so much that, given a first line, they cannot help but write the next one. It makes new things by recombining everything it has ever seen. The result feels creative because it is memory, reshuffled at speed. It is prediction pushed forward — each next word, or pixel, guessed from everything that came before it. That next-word, next-stroke magic is Few-Shot Examples.
